items.title: BAPS and its celibate monks: The organisation at the centre of the Eiffel Tower row
items.summary: A Hindu religious organisation has come under fire in Paris, France after female employees at the Eiffel Tower were allegedly asked to move away or make themselves “invisible” during a private visit by its delegation. This prompted staff to strike and force the iconic landmark to close on September 7. The delegation, comprising around 100 people, was from the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha, or BAPS, a Hindu religious organisation with roots in Gujarat and a large global following. French authorities are investigating the incident after employees said they were instructed to make themselves “invisible” while the delegation passed through the landmark. BAPS is a denomination within the Swaminarayan tradition of Hinduism. A Hindu group with several branches in the UK and US it gets millions in donations and grants every year. Recently, the massive BAPS Swaminarayan temple in Paris was inaugurated. Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the inauguration through a video message and described the temple as a milestone in India-France cultural relations. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay is facing strong criticism from the Opposition Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) over a gesture he made while referring to former Chief Minister and DMK president MK Stalin’s detention during the Emergency under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA). The DMK accused Vijay of mocking the facial stiffness Stalin reportedly developed as a result of police brutality following his detention during the Emergency. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], which extends external support to the government, also criticised the Chief Minister’s gesture. Vijay made the gesture while replying to the demands for grants for the Police and Fire and Rescue Services departments in the Assembly on Monday. He departed from his prepared speech to attack the DMK during the debate. “They (DMK) always say they have seen the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA). items.title: Opinion: Mohan Bhagwat’s speech on oneness barely hides his Hindutva sophistry
items.summary: Several press reports and prominent commentators on Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat’s speech at New York’s Madison Square Garden tell us that his words on ‘oneness in diversity’ mark a welcome departure from hardline Hindu supremacism. Others believe that Bhagwat has given the RSS a liberal spin in the US, in words he would not use in India. Both these assessments are off the mark. Bhagwat has given near-identical speeches several times in India, including earlier this year. Indeed he told his US audience as much, recalling his 2018 speech given at Nagpur. He uses the same formulations in both the US and India, but in the latter, he is more expansive. Place one next to the other, and the Hindu supremacist sophistry becomes unmistakeable. ‘Oneness’ vs ‘unity’ The concept of ‘universal oneness’ can mean that all beings, all things, and all spiritual traditions are equally valid expressions of the same perennial philosophy, the same inner oneness. It would follow that the Hindu traditions too would be one among such diverse expressions. But that’s not what Bhagwat said.
